reply.text:
Training can help, but not in the way you're hoping. It won't undo a day you went over, because the number on any single day isn't what moves your results. What training can do is give you something to measure besides the scale and the calorie count: a lift going up, a run feeling easier, a streak you built. That tends to loosen the grip of the numbers.

The panic is a separate thing from the training. If going over a number sets off real distress, that's worth talking through with a doctor or a dietitian, since they handle exactly this kind of relationship with food. I can't treat it, but I can keep your training steady and give you goals that aren't about eating less.

Want me to look at where your lifts and goals stand so we can pick something to chase besides the log?
